transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I guess… what brings me in is I just don’t feel much real happiness anymore. I mean, things are okay on paper, and I try not to make a big deal of it, but even when my wife wants us to do our old Sunday routines, or something good happens at work, I can’t really feel close or enjoy it the way I used to. It’s like I’m going through the motions. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way, going through the motions without really feeling happiness or connection?

It’s been… I guess longer than I wanted to admit. Since the retrofit accident, really. That was about a year and seven months ago. I kept thinking it would pass, you know, that I’d get back to normal, but it’s kind of stayed with me.
Since the accident, have you experienced periods where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless most of the day, nearly every day. I mean… I have bad stretches, sure, but I’m still getting up and doing what I’m supposed to do. So, I don’t know if it fits what you’re asking exactly.
Have you noticed that you no longer take pleasure in, or look forward to, activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I still do the things, you know, like the Sunday stuff with my wife, and I try to act like I’m into it. And if something goes well at work, I know I should feel good about it.

But it’s just… muted, I guess. I don’t really look forward to things the same way, and when they’re happening I don’t feel that happiness or closeness like I used to. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but that’s probably one of the main reasons I came in.
Have you noticed that you feel fatigued or that you’ve lost your energy, even when you haven’t done much physically or mentally?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly noticed that, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, work and life and all that, but I’m not sure it’s been this separate thing where I have no energy for no reason.

Maybe I haven’t been paying attention to it the right way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t think it’s been most of the day, nearly every day, no. I mean, I’ve had low moments, and I’m not exactly cheerful, but “depressed most of the day” feels… stronger than what I’d say.

I’m trying to answer it the way you mean it, not just brush it off. But over the last couple weeks, I wouldn’t say that’s been constant like that.
Can you describe how often you’ve felt a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like the Sunday routines with your wife or work achievements?

It’s… pretty often, honestly. I still show up for those things, like Sundays with my wife, and I try not to make it obvious because she’s trying. I don’t want her to feel like it’s her fault.

But the real happiness, or that closeness I used to feel, it just doesn’t really come. Same with work—if something goes well, I can recognize it’s good, and I’ll say the right thing, but I don’t feel much from it. That’s actually a big part of why I thought I should talk to someone. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Can you tell me if you’ve had days where you feel down or low for most of the day, and if so, how often does that happen?

I’m not totally sure I’d call it “most of the day.” I do have days where I feel low, but it kind of comes and goes, or I can push through it if I’m busy.

I don’t want to overstate it. Maybe a few days here and there? But I haven’t really tracked it closely, so I’m not sure I can give you a clean number. Is that okay as an answer?
Can you tell me if there have been times when you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, and if so, how long did that last?

I’m not sure I can say that it’s been nearly every day for a stretch, no. There have been times where I’ve felt pretty low for a good part of the day, but I don’t think I’ve had, like, two weeks straight where it was most of the day every day.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just because I’m trying to be agreeable. I’d say it’s more intermittent than constant, if that makes sense.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms have persisted for over two years (since the accident 1 year and 7 months ago) with a chronic, less severe mood disturbance that does not meet the full criteria for a major depressive episode (as the patient denies persistent sadness most of the day nearly every day for a sustained period). This aligns with the diagnosis of dysthymia (F34.1). Other depressive episode codes (F32.0–F33.9) are ruled out due to insufficient severity or duration for those categories.
